note_claims.claim: The patient has had diarrhoea and vomiting for two days.
The patient has experienced vomiting twice this morning and nothing since lunch.
The patient has had four to five loose stools today.
The patient has no blood in her stools.
The patient experiences crampy abdominal pain before defecation.
The patient has poor oral intake.
The patient last passed dark urine this morning.
The patient had a fall last month.
The patient has a sore on her left heel.
The patient is taking Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily.
The patient is taking Ramipril 5 mg once daily.
The patient is taking Furosemide 40 mg once daily (corrected from initial mention of two tablets).
The patient is taking Atorvastatin at night.
The consultation was a telephone consultation and no physical examination was performed.
The clinical impression is probable infective gastroenteritis with dehydration in an 85-year-old on metformin, an ACE inhibitor, and a loop diuretic, with a risk of acute kidney injury.
The plan is to administer small, frequent fluids and oral rehydration sachets.
A U&E blood test is scheduled for tomorrow, to be taken by the district nurse during the heel dressing visit.
The patient should call 111 or 999 if she is unable to keep fluids down, becomes confused or very drowsy, passes no urine for 12 hours, or sees blood in her diarrhoea.
